events.title: Pope Gregory XIII Issues the Calendar Reform
events.description: Pope Gregory XIII issued the papal bull Inter gravissimas, which introduced a revised calendar to correct the drift of the Julian calendar. The reform changed the leap-year rules and dropped ten days to realign the calendar with the seasons.
events.significance: The Gregorian calendar is now the most widely used civil calendar in the world.

events.title: Marbury v. Madison Decided
events.description: The U.S. Supreme Court, led by Chief Justice John Marshall, ruled in Marbury v. Madison. It held that part of the Judiciary Act of 1789 was unconstitutional.
events.significance: The decision established judicial review, the power of American courts to strike down laws that conflict with the Constitution.

events.title: Birth of Steve Jobs
events.description: Steve Jobs was born in San Francisco, California. He went on to co-found Apple and to lead the company's later work on the iPod, iPhone and iPad.
events.significance: Jobs helped shape personal computing, digital music and mobile devices, and changed how people use technology every day.

events.title: Russia Launches Full-Scale Invasion of Ukraine
events.description: Russian forces attacked Ukraine from several directions, widening a conflict that had begun in 2014. The offensive set off a major war in Europe and a large refugee crisis.
events.significance: It was the largest military conflict in Europe since World War II, and it reshaped global security, energy markets and international alliances.
